edges.reason: msg.sender is written into the owner state variable in the Owned constructor.
transferOwnership is gated by onlyOwner, which compares msg.sender against owner.
acceptOwnership requires the caller msg.sender to equal newOwner.
transfer debits and credits using the caller-controlled msg.sender balance key.
approve writes the allowance under the caller-controlled msg.sender key.
transferFrom spends allowed[from][msg.sender], keyed by the untrusted caller.
approveAndCall grants the allowance to msg.sender and passes msg.sender into receiveApproval.
The onlyOwner require compares the untrusted msg.sender against owner.
The acceptOwnership require compares the untrusted msg.sender against newOwner.
safeAdd performs c = a + b guarded by require(c >= a).
safeSub performs c = a - b guarded by require(b <= a).
safeMul performs c = a * b guarded by require(a == 0 || c / a == b).
safeDiv performs c = a / b guarded by require(b > 0).
approveAndCall executes an external call to spender.receiveApproval while state has already been updated.
transferAnyERC20Token performs an external call to an arbitrary token contract.
transferOwnership is protected by the onlyOwner modifier check.
acceptOwnership enforces the caller check against newOwner.
A malicious spender contract can re-enter approveAndCall from receiveApproval. Callback edge where vuln_type is reentrancy.
A malicious tokenAddress can call back into transferAnyERC20Token during the external transfer. Callback edge where vuln_type is reentrancy.
transfer uses safeSub to debit the sender balance.
transfer uses safeAdd to credit the recipient balance.
transferFrom uses safeSub on the source balance and on the allowance.
transferFrom uses safeAdd to credit the recipient balance.
Owned constructor writes owner.
transferOwnership writes newOwner.
acceptOwnership overwrites owner with newOwner.
acceptOwnership clears newOwner to address(0).
